$comment: The plate layout a Realistic world's seed draws (docs/proposals/REALISTIC_WORLD.md §3.1, phase R1; owner 2026-11-11: plates decide land and sea, face B its own plates from its own face seed). Read by crates/dwell-worldgen/src/plates.rs; not wired into any world yet, so nothing here changes the terrain a seed generates. `count` [min, max]: the seed picks how many plates (3–5 for the first region, the proposal's default; Q1 not answered). `reach`: plates and hotspots lie within this many m of the disc's centre, and the layout covers that disc; `seaMargin`: the outer m of it are sea whatever the plate (the disc must end in sea). `spacing`: the least distance between two plates' centres (m), tried at up to `attempts` seeded points. `kinds`: each plate kind (code vocabulary: oceanic, continental) has a draw `weight` and a `min` count the layout keeps (oceanic plate = sea, continental = land). `speed` [min, max] cm/yr and `age` [min, max] Myr are drawn uniformly per plate. `warp`: the boundaries curve by `amplitude` m of noise at `wavelength` m. `transformBelow`: a boundary is transform where the closing (or opening) rate across it is less than this share of the plates' relative speed, else convergent (closing) or divergent (opening). `hotspots`: `count` [min, max] points fixed in the mantle within `within` m of the centre; the chain runs back along the overlying plate's motion. `fixtures`: two-plate layouts by data with the boundary each must give (`kind`, and `subducts`: the index of the plate that dives, or null) — the tests check every entry. Run `node shared/worldgen/gen.mjs` after editing; CI fails on stale output.
